Three-step diagram of the capture–recapture method in a pond, arranged left to right with arrows. Step 1: a net catching several Tilapia fish, with a counter showing the first sample. Step 2: the same fish each given a small coloured mark on the fin and released back into the pond, mixing with unmarked fish. Step 3: a second net catch containing mostly unmarked fish and a few marked fish (marked ones highlighted). Below, the formula box. Soft blues and greens.

A graph-like diagram comparing natural succession with a plagioclimax. A staircase of vegetation stages rising from left to right (bare soil, weeds, grasses, shrubs, young trees, climax forest) labelled with an arrow reaching the top. A second path branches off at the grass stage and stays flat, with small flame icons and grazing cattle showing repeated bush burning and grazing holding the vegetation at the grass stage. Soft greens, yellows and orange.

A grassy school field seen from above with a grid of faint lines. Several 1 m square wooden quadrat frames lie at random positions, each containing a few small Tridax plants (yellow-centred flowers) drawn as dots. One quadrat is enlarged in a circle at the side showing 4 plants counted inside it. A student with a notebook stands beside the field. Soft greens and browns.

Two panels illustrating niche differentiation. Left: a tall tree divided into horizontal zones by dashed lines, with a different small insect-eating bird feeding in each zone (top canopy, middle branches near the trunk, lower branches, forest floor). Right: a savanna scene with a tall zebra eating the tops of tall grass, a wildebeest eating the middle parts and a small gazelle eating short shoots near the ground; in the background, a goat standing on its hind legs browsing a shrub and cattle grazing grass. Soft greens, browns and yellows.

A horizontal sequence of seven panels showing primary succession on bare rock in a tropical setting, each panel slightly later in time and joined by arrows. (1) Bare grey rock under a hot sun. (2) The rock with patches of grey-green and orange crusty lichens and tiny cracks. (3) Green cushions of moss growing in a thin layer of dark soil in cracks. (4) Ferns, small herbs and grasses in thicker soil. (5) Bushy shrubs among the grasses. (6) Young trees overtopping the shrubs. (7) A tall, dense climax forest with several layers. Under each panel, a strip showing the soil layer getting deeper from none to thick. A long arrow beneath. Soft greys, greens and browns.

A horizontal sequence of six panels showing secondary succession on abandoned farmland in southern Nigeria, joined by arrows. (1) A recently harvested farm with bare soil, old yam mounds and a few tree stumps. (2) Short annual weeds with small yellow and white flowers (Tridax, goat weed) covering the soil. (3) Tall spear grass and guinea grass with Siam weed shrubs. (4) Bushy shrubs and coppice shoots from old stumps rising above the grass. (5) Young secondary forest with umbrella trees (Musanga) with large hand-shaped leaves and oil palms. (6) Tall, dense climax rainforest. A long arrow beneath. Soft greens and browns.

Two population growth graphs side by side, both with "time" on the horizontal axis and "number of individuals (population size)" on the vertical axis. Left: an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve with five shaded and labelled phases from left to right: lag phase (flat start), exponential (log) phase (steep rise), deceleration phase (bending), stationary phase (flat plateau), and a slight downward death phase at the end. A dashed horizontal line at the plateau labelled carrying capacity (K). Right: a J-shaped curve rising slowly and then very steeply, followed by a sudden sharp drop (crash). Soft blue and soft green lines.

Three population (age) pyramids side by side, each a horizontal bar chart with age groups (0–4 at the bottom up to 80+ at the top) on a central vertical axis, males on the left in soft blue and females on the right in soft pink. Left: expanding pyramid with a very broad base and a narrow peak. Middle: stable pyramid with nearly straight vertical sides narrowing only near the top. Right: contracting pyramid with a narrower base than its middle. Nigeria)", "stable", "contracting (e.g. Japan)", "males", "females", "age group", "high birth rate", "low birth rate", "young people", "old people".

Four cross-sections of the same pond over time, left to right, joined by arrows, showing a hydrosere. (1) Open pond with phytoplankton and submerged plants and a thin layer of mud. (2) Shallower pond with water lilies and floating plants and thicker mud. (3) Mostly filled marsh with reeds, sedges and Typha spreading inwards and a small pool left. (4) Dry land with grasses, shrubs and young trees, and a forest in the background. Soft blues, greens and browns.
